holes_read.note: This practice's reading of the twenty empty cells the arithmetic finds most surprising, 2026-09-08. The exact probability ranks them; nothing in the data says why any of them is empty. Each verdict below is a judgment made by reading the two words and then checking one contingency in the feed, and each names the check. Four labels were available: `vocabulary` (the combination is a contradiction in the catalogue's own words), `assignment` (one field's value is handed out along with the other, so the pair cannot vary), `collection` (the cell is empty because of which source supplied that part of the catalogue), and `candidate` (nothing above explains it, so it may be a combination nobody has made). The count of `candidate` is the number that matters, and it is zero.

reading.title: Anatomy of an AI System
reading.reason: 'invisible' names the hidden material cost of infrastructure, not a record that was never made
reading.move: Traces the full extractive supply chain of a single Amazon Echo — minerals, ghost labor, data, disposal — into one exploded-view diagram/essay, converting AI's invisible material costs into a legible map, published online and printed as a large-format poster.

reading.title: Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Technology and Power, 1500–2025
reading.reason: 'refusing' names a myth about AI's origins, not uncollected data
reading.move: A 24-metre hand-drawn genealogical map tracing extraction, classification and computation from 1500 to the present, refusing the 'AI arrived from nowhere' myth by making five centuries of power visible in one unbroken line.

reading.title: LAUREN
reading.reason: 'invisible' is the hidden human labour behind a device
reading.move: The artist replaces Amazon Alexa's algorithm with her own body: for three days she personally, remotely watches a household 24/7 through installed cameras and mics and operates its locks and faucets by hand — making the ordinarily invisible human labor and surveillance behind 'smart home AI' fully visible and answerable to one named person.

reading.title: Life Support System (aka. The Farm)
reading.reason: 'invisible' is an unpriced subsidy, not an absent record
reading.move: One square metre of wheat grown indoors under full automated instrumentation — every watt, litre and nutrient metered live — reveals a true production cost of roughly 200 EUR/kg versus a 15-cent market price, making an invisible ecosystem subsidy legible. Note: sourced page does not itself frame this as an AI/ML work (it is automated environmental monitoring rather than machine learning); included

reading.title: Machine Hallucinations – Satellite Simulations: B
reading.reason: 'invisible' is the compute cost hidden behind a spectacle
reading.move: Trains AI on vast satellite/Earth-observation datasets to generate an immersive, hypnotic 'data sublime' on an 8.5×6 m LED wall — the material and energetic cost of that compute stays invisible behind the spectacle it produces.

reading.title: Newly Forgotten Technologies
reading.reason: 'forgotten' is obsolescence of hardware, not a gap in a dataset
reading.move: A sound-art graveyard of defunct Alexa-style voice assistants staged as an artefact from a near future where 'smart' devices have already died — a memento mori for AI hardware's short life and long e-waste tail.

reading.title: Sensing Streams – invisible, inaudible
reading.reason: 'invisible' is the electromagnetic substrate made perceptible
reading.move: Captures ambient electromagnetic waves (80MHz–5.2GHz) from wifi, cell signals and broadcast infrastructure in real time and converts them into synchronised sound and light, making the invisible material substrate of 'wireless' data physically perceptible.

reading.title: The Great Bare Mat and Constellation
reading.reason: 'invisible' is network traffic materialised, and the traffic is recorded
reading.move: A hand-woven carpet's pattern is generated by literally plotting the Collective's own internet traffic over one hour onto the star-map of Ursa Major, materializing invisible network data exchange as a domestic, walkable object.

reading.title: Terra Ex Machina
reading.artist: Hagit Keysar & Ariel Caine (with Barak Brinker)
reading.reason: 'invisible' is an algorithmic boundary, which the work makes legible from data that exists
reading.move: Deliberately crashes drones into an invisible algorithmic 'geofence' restricting flight over Jerusalem's Old City, then rebuilds aerial imagery with residents via DIY balloons and kites to make the boundary and its data politics legible.

reading.title: A Disappeared Movement
reading.reason: evasion of surveillance, not a missing record
reading.move: Mapped and measured the viewing angle of 89 surveillance cameras along an 1,100-metre Beijing street, then choreographed a zigzagging walk that stays permanently outside their combined field of view.

reading.title: Biblioteca de la No-Historia (Library of Non-History)
reading.reason: the redaction blackouts of a declassified archive are the work's material: what the record withholds
reading.move: A thousand hand-bound books reproduce declassified CIA files (via the U.S. National Security Archive / FOIA) on Operation Condor and Southern Cone dictatorships — the seals, stamps, and redaction blackouts of the originals kept intact, so the archive's own censorship becomes the artwork's visible content.

reading.title: Cumulus
reading.reason: 'invisible' is a border unseen from orbit; the satellite data exist
reading.move: A CubeSat-inspired networked device continuously pulls real NOAA weather-satellite feeds to track clouds crossing the Mexico-US border, using an actual open dataset to make visible how a border invisible from orbit is nonetheless rigidly enforced on the ground.

reading.title: Data Against Feminicide
reading.artist: Catherine D'Ignazio, Silvana Fumega, Helena Suárez Val (MIT Data + Feminism Lab, ILDA, Feminicidio Uruguay)
reading.reason: builds counterdata for the body-counting states do not do — the dataset's absence is the premise
reading.move: Networks 180+ grassroots feminicide-monitoring groups across the Americas and co-designs an AI news-alert system (scanning 50,000+ outlets via Media Cloud) that performs the body-counting states refuse to do — counterdata as activist infrastructure, not an academic dataset.

reading.title: Digital Violence: How the NSO Group Enables State Terror
reading.artist: Forensic Architecture, with Amnesty International and Citizen Lab
reading.reason: 'invisible' spyware infrastructure made legible from forensic data that exists
reading.move: Maps forensic phone-analysis data from Amnesty and Citizen Lab onto a navigable platform combining sonified data, victim testimonies and a corporate-affiliation diagram — makes NSO Group's invisible spyware infrastructure spatially and sonically legible.

reading.title: Herbicidal Warfare in Gaza
reading.artist: Forensic Architecture (with Al Mezan Center, Gisha, Adalah)
reading.reason: 'invisible' is a herbicide cloud reconstructed from imagery that exists
reading.move: Uses satellite imagery, wind-drift modeling, and testimony to prove that Israeli aerial herbicide spraying along the Gaza border destroyed Palestinian farmland hundreds of metres deep into the territory, turning an invisible atmospheric 'cloud' into legally actionable evidence.

reading.title: kith and kin
reading.reason: built from redacted coronial files on deaths in custody — what the state's record does not say
reading.move: Hand-chalked genealogical chart tracing 65,000 years and thousands of relatives directly from government archives, court/conviction records, and redacted coronial files on 557 Aboriginal deaths in custody since 1991, suspended over a reflecting pool of the source documents themselves.

reading.title: Networks of New York: An Illustrated Field Guide to Urban Internet Infrastructure
reading.reason: 'invisible' is buried infrastructure, mapped from what is there
reading.move: An illustrated field guide decoding New York's buried internet infrastructure — manhole-cover codes, carrier hotels, sidewalk spray-paint markings — turning invisible network geography into a walkable, annotatable map.

reading.title: Saydnaya (the missing 19dB)
reading.reason: no images of the prison exist; the work reconstructs from that absence
reading.move: Since no images exist of Syria's secret Saydnaya prison, reconstructs its acoustic conditions purely from survivors' sound memories — turning forced visual deprivation and echo-measurement into courtroom-deployable forensic evidence for Amnesty International.

reading.title: 97 Empleadas Domésticas (97 Domestic Employees)
reading.reason: the worker structurally excluded from the frame she sustains — the omission is the subject
reading.move: 97 photographs scraped from upper-class Peruvian families' Facebook albums are re-presented for what each one accidentally documents at its margins: a cropped hand, a shadow, a domestic worker structurally excluded from the frame she materially sustains — consent-free data repurposed to expose exactly the erasure it originally performed.

reading.title: Not the Only One (N'TOO)
reading.reason: refuses existing datasets and builds a family corpus instead; about inadequate data rather than absent data
reading.move: Trains a sculptural voice-AI oracle exclusively on oral histories from three generations of the artist's own Black family, refusing commercial datasets she considers irreparably biased — the AI's glitches and refusals become deliberate pedagogy about data sovereignty rather than bugs to be fixed.

reading.title: Once Upon A Garden (Once Upon a Flower series)
reading.reason: flora that colonial archival gaps 'already erased or never recorded'
reading.move: Builds her own GAN training sets from photographed Senegalese flowers and scanned national-archive material — rejecting biased large Western models — to speculatively generate flora that global warming and colonial archival gaps have already erased or never recorded.

reading.title: She Who Sees the Unknown
reading.reason: erased and demonised figures rebuilt into an archive that did not hold them
reading.move: 3D-scans and 3D-prints erased or demonized female/queer jinn figures from Middle Eastern mythology, pairing physical sculptures with an open digital archive and storytelling practice she names 'Re-Figuring' — coining and theorizing 'digital colonialism' as a critical framework for whose myths and data get to persist.

reading.title: Venenosas, Nocivas e Suspeitas
reading.reason: erased women botanists, and the naming system that dropped them
reading.move: Three years of AI-generated fictional plants and portraits of erased women botanists expose the sexism and colonialism embedded in plant nomenclature; asked to depict aging women accurately, the AI systems balked at rendering wrinkles — their bias becoming part of the evidence on display.

reading.title: A Nation Is a Massacre
reading.reason: missing and murdered Indigenous people recited as a register the state does not keep
reading.move: A large-format text installation that lists/recites five centuries of massacres, missing and murdered Indigenous people, and environmental-racism incidents as a confrontational, register-like data litany covering a gallery floor and walls.

reading.title: Barbed Wire Village
reading.artist: Chao Tayiana Maina / Museum of British Colonialism
reading.reason: detention camps the post-independence archive had erased, rebuilt from survivor data
reading.move: 3D-reconstructs suppressed British 'villagisation' and Mau Mau detention camps from archival and survivor data, rebuilding a physical Nairobi exhibition around a digitally modeled colonial crime scene that Kenya's post-independence archive had erased.

reading.title: Breathing with the Forest
reading.reason: 'invisible' is ecological reciprocity made perceptible from measured data
reading.move: Builds an architectural-scale, 3-channel immersive visualization around real carbon, water and mycorrhizal-network data drawn from a single Capinuri tree in the Colombian Amazon, making invisible more-than-human ecological reciprocity perceptible - though its sublime, cinematic staging leans closer to spectacle than to a data-justice argument.

reading.title: Masakhane
reading.reason: languages historically excluded from models; the community builds the missing datasets
reading.move: A distributed, no-prerequisite community ('we build together' in isiZulu) crowdsources open datasets, translation and speech models for African languages historically excluded from big tech's language models — treating linguistic decolonization as ongoing collective infrastructure-building rather than a single authored work.

reading.title: Meditation on Country
reading.artist: Angie Abdilla, with Ghillar Michael Anderson, Brian Schmidt and Katie Noon
reading.reason: 'refusing' a single default cosmology, not a gap in a record
reading.move: An immersive film installation uses machine learning to stage Aboriginal ancestral deep-time knowledge and Western astrophysics side by side under a simulated sky — refusing to let AI default to a single, Western epistemology of the cosmos.

reading.title: The REDress Project
reading.reason: empty dresses stand for an uncounted statistical gap — absence made spatial
reading.move: Empty red dresses (400+, many donated by families) hung in public sites across North America to make the uncounted statistical gap of missing and murdered Indigenous women viscerally, spatially present as absence.

reading.title: Yanmeeyarr
reading.reason: ceremony translated to light; no claim about a missing record
reading.move: Ochre body-marking patterns used in Gunditjmara ceremony, translated into a light-and-shadow installation across the museum's ceiling, framing the threshold visitors cross into and out of a history of the moving image.

reading.title: Data Feminism
reading.reason: turns 'whose voice is missing from the data' into a method
reading.move: Reframes data science through intersectional feminist theory, arguing that counting and classification themselves encode power — turns 'whose voice is missing from the data' into a repeatable analytic method rather than a moral aside.

reading.title: Here the River Lies
reading.reason: oral micro-histories of a vanished river, indexed where no archive holds them
reading.move: Crowdsources 1,500+ oral micro-histories of a vanished river onto a hand-drawn map and deliberately refuses to distinguish verified memory from invented story, indexing both into the same archive as a challenge to the evidentiary claims of official heritage data.

reading.title: Minotauros (Minotaurs)
reading.reason: workers who accumulate no data trail — missing data made to move
reading.move: An 8-bit-aesthetic LED labyrinth animates Mexico City's informal-economy occupation rate — rendering, in low-resolution video-game imagery, the workers who accumulate no data trail toward a pension: missing data made visibly to move.

reading.title: Missing Datasets (list/essay)
reading.reason: a list of datasets that go uncollected
reading.move: An open, continually-added public list plus essay cataloguing real-world datasets that go uncollected, giving the physical Library's concept a living, crowd-legible digital counterpart.

reading.title: Sobrevivientes
reading.artist: Datasketch (with Sandra Suárez / QueremosDatos.co, Data Against Feminicide network)
reading.reason: denied complete records, builds its own and renders the state's non-counting
reading.move: Denied complete femicide records through freedom-of-information requests, the team built its own database from news reports and survivor testimony, then translated the gaps into embroidery, illustration, digital maps, and a public-space intervention — data activism that makes the state's non-counting visible.

reading.title: The Library of Missing Datasets
reading.reason: empty labelled folders: structural absence as the exhibit
reading.move: A literal filing cabinet of empty, labeled folders — each naming a dataset that societies choose not to collect (e.g. undocumented migrants incarcerated in the US) — makes structural absence itself the exhibit.

reading.title: The Library of Missing Datasets (v2.0)
reading.reason: the same, in its second version, naming datasets that structurally do not exist
reading.move: Fills steel filing cabinets with empty folders labeled by the names of datasets that structurally do not exist ('People excluded from housing due to criminal records', 'Uncounted deaths tied to Hurricane Maria') — making data's absence itself the exhibit, by a Nigerian-American artist working at the intersection of data collection and racial/social omission.

reading.title: un- (anterior ellipse[s] as mangled container; or where edges meet to wedge and [un]moor)
reading.reason: refusal as a political posture in a sculptural restaging, not about a record
reading.move: Six panes of dark glass suspended at a threatening angle over visitors' heads, restaging the 1964 CORE 'stall-in' protest as a physical mechanics of surveillance and Black refusal — power made into a literal ceiling.

reading.title: Vigil
reading.reason: names of missing women against an unresolved case count
reading.move: A durational street performance — scrubbing the pavement, yelling the first names of real missing women written on her arms, then nailing a red dress to a pole until it tears — marking the unresolved case count of over 65 missing Downtown Eastside women.

reading.title: DATALAND
reading.artist: Refik Anadol Studio (Refik Anadol & Efsun Erkılıç)
reading.reason: 'anonymized' describes the work's own data handling
reading.move: A permanent 25,000 sq ft museum where a wristband ('Empathica') and scent-diffusing neckband feed anonymized visitor biometric/behavioral signals back into generative rainforest-data visuals — data spectacle fully institutionalized as a standing museum genre rather than a temporary blockbuster stunt.

reading.move: composition crudely representing a future newspaper headline lamenting the failure of the show it was featured at due to the absence of work by the artist

reading.move: in the late-twentieth and early-twenty first centuries. By preserving artifacts and memorabilia, Rosales tells the stories of communities often underrepresented

reading.reason: the description says nothing about the work; the title alone cannot decide it
reading.move: what belongs to the spectrum of one's history: subjective or objective, microscopic or macroscopic, private, familial, and socio-political. Through my work

reading.reason: 'forgotten' is a nostalgic web aesthetic
reading.move: almost forgotten web that is loud, colorful, often "personal", and doesn't care about standards. Though it might be forgotten by many, some parts of it are

reading.title: Untangler
reading.reason: African perspectives absent from training data, named as the asymmetry the work works on
reading.move: Artificial intelligence systems are not neutral. Trained predominantly on Western datasets, they carry a fundamental asymmetry: African perspectives are absent, misrepresented, or subsumed beneath colonial inheritance.

reading.reason: Iraqi dead who are uncounted in the American record, tattooed as dots
reading.move: Wafaa Bilal’s brother, Haji, was killed by a missile at a checkpoint in their hometown of Kufa, Iraq in 2004. reading.title: THE DELUSION
reading.reason: censorship is a theme of a game, not a missing dataset
reading.move: THE DELUSION is a multiplayer immersive experience that combines cooperative gaming and participatory theatre to explore themes of polarisation, censorship and social connection.

reading.title: VRJ Palestine
reading.reason: reconstructs demolished villages from archives and testimony; about destroyed places more than an absent record
reading.move: The VRJ Palestine initiative (Virtual Reality Journey to pre-Nakba Palestine) delves into the potential and challenges of Virtual Reality tools to reclaim and recapture Nakba’s lost landscapes. Using archival data and survivors’ accounts to virtually reconstruct the Palestinian villages demolished in 1948, it aims to preserve intergenerational memories conveyed through stories and photos.

reading.title: Prometheus Firebringer
reading.reason: generates versions of a lost play — a missing text rather than missing data
reading.move: Prometheus Firebringer is a lecture-performance about generative AI, technology and power. On the performance side, the predictive text model GPT-4 generates speculative versions of the lost final play of Aeschylus’ Prometheia trilogy. Each night, a chorus of AI-generated Greek masks performs a new iteration. On the lecture side, Dorsen delivers a talk made up entirely…

reading.artist: Rojava Center for Democratic Technologies, Dani Ploeger
reading.reason: 'absence' is of refrigeration, not of data
reading.move: ‘European-style’ refrigerators can only be operated with a large solar system that costs the equivalent of a year’s income or more. Especially during the extreme summer heat, the absence of adequate cooling systems has detrimental effects on the quality of life. At the same time, many people are not keen to explore alternatives that are…

reading.title: AI in the Sky
reading.reason: 'classified' is a taxonomic status of a plant
reading.move: At the heart of this project is a plant so rare that it stands on the brink of extinction. This plant, the Encephalartos woodii (E. woodii), a cycad classified as ‘extinct in the wild,’ is known from a single pollen-producing specimen found in South Africa’s oNgoye Forest in the late 19th century.

reading.title: Performative Ethnographies
reading.reason: exclusion of people from a process, not from a record
reading.move: Performative Ethnographies (PE) are an artistic methodology and ongoing non-disciplinary research created as a response to the multiple layers of exclusion of laypeople from spaces where advanced technology is developed, even though their bodies are affected by it.

reading_note: This practice's own reading of every entry either screen flagged, 2026-09-08. A verdict answers one question: is this work about data that was never collected, erased, or refused — as opposed to data that exists and is merely hard to see? The verdicts are a judgment, not a measurement, and they are committed so that anyone can disagree with a named one. 'borderline' is used where the entry's own words do not settle it.
